The result shows that the rooftops of SUT are efficiency. 38 buildings were considered and the result of economics study shows that NPV is Positive, IRR is more than minimum loan rate, B/C Ratio is more than one, DPB is 9.3 years, LCOE is 1.94 baht/unit, and the Sensitivity scenario demonstrates the cost reduction in an installation from 50 to 45 baht/watt. To sum up, the project is quite interesting to invest.

articleTitle: A study of 3D-printed carbon electrodes for the manufacture of electric double-layer capacitors
abstract: Screen printing, inkjet printing, doctor blade coating and dip coating are among the most common methods that have been developed and researched for the manufacture of supercapacitors. A more recent method to emerge in this field is 3D printing. This research investigates the most effective concentration of carbon conductive paint (CCP) for 3D printing electrodes and current collectors for small cuboidal electric double layer capacitors (EDLCs). The precise CCP used for experiments was Bare Conductive Electric Paint. CCP is designed to create custom conductive surfaces and is compatible with 3D printing. The EDLC samples were produced using a combination of two well-established 3D printing techniques. Several 1.0 mm thick EDLC samples were produced with varying concentrations of CCP to compare electrical performance and printing feasibility. Electrical performance and printability was found to be impacted by the carbon concentration of the CCP. Lower carbon concentrations limited the conductivity of the components printed, while higher concentrations were too viscous to be printed. A ratio of 0.3:3.0 parts CCP to distilled water (specifically 3.0 g CCP and 3 g distilled water) was found to optimize electrical performance of samples that could feasibly be 3D-printed.

articleTitle: Innovative Materials for Transformer of the Future
abstract: Transformers of the future will be solid state, dry type and designed to meet the requirements of the smart grid. The materials used for producing these transformers will have to meet the criteria of low losses, high thermal endurance etc. This paper reviews the present status of the development of these materials and the emerging trends of technological development of new materials, including active power conversion materials, magnetic materials, conducting materials and insulation materials.

articleTitle: Considering the Design and Operation of a Voice Controlled Laboratory for Teaching and Learning in Electronic Engineering
abstract: In this paper, the design and operation of a voice controlled electronic engineering laboratory for the teaching and learning of semiconductor device current-voltage (IV) characteristics are presented. This is targeted to students studying electronic engineering in a higher education setting. The presented case study experiment operation, based on a Schottky diode forward and reverse bias IV characteristics, is presented. This uses a computer-based interface to an Arduino UNO platform that acts as the experiment test and measurement equipment. The computer side software developed is based on a Python script along with a speech recognition library and the online Google Speech Recognition service for identifying voice commands.

articleTitle: A Novel Trade-off Management for Energy Storage System in Microgrid System
abstract: This paper presents a novel trade-off management for an energy storage system (ESS) in the microgrid system; the main aim for peak load shaving in the secondary distribution system. The IEEE 123 node test feeder was used to implement the ESS under unbalanced power flow. The comparison of each case showed that the impact of the installed ESS into the microgrid was related to the control scheme of the ESS and installed location. The results showed that the optimal ESS location was node No.60 under minimal energy loss. Meanwhile, the trade-off control could use two points of peak shaving reduction. Therefore, the ESS needs to be optimally implemented in real-time control studies in the future.

articleTitle: Fault Cause Classification on PEA 33 kV Distribution System using Supervised Machine Learning compared to Artificial Neural Network
abstract: A fault occurring in a distribution system has low reliability. Therefore, when a fault occurs, the system restoration should have the fastest. The purpose of this article is to develop an algorithm to classify the cause of faults in Provincial Electricity Authority (PEA.) distribution systems in southern area 2 of Thailand with waveform characterization and compares the performance of the supervised machine learning (SML) and the artificial neural network (ANN) technique to reduce the outage duration. The characteristic signature of voltage and current waveform i.e., voltage dip, rate of change of current and voltage, neutral current and voltage, temporary or permanent fault, fault type, and evolving fault were extracted, provided to SML and ANN to classify the cause of faults focusing on animals, tree contact, and equipment failure. Accuracy testing of the algorithm by real testing was performed with the distribution system of PEA in the central-southern area of Thailand. The result shows that when the group of fault events is correctly classified, the proposed method can provide the high accuracy of identifying fault cause with the lowest ML accuracy of 81.21% and the lowest ANN accuracy of 62.50%. Consequently, In the condition of this paper, the SML can classify more accurately than the ANN.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Dual-Band Power Dividers Based on Conjugately Characteristic-Impedance Transmission Lines (CCITLs)
abstract: A miniaturized dual-band power divider for microwave frequencies has been developed. The present design utilizes the two-section impedance transformers implemented by the conjugately characteristic-impedance transmission lines (CCITL) to obtain size reduction with dual-band characteristic. The properly designed CCITL can achieve shorter electrical length than the normal transmission line (TL) to provide the same impedance transformation characteristic. Approximately one-fourth size reduction has been achieved by the proposed technique with reasonable results of scattering parameters, as compared with the similar design using the two-section impedance transformers but realized by the normal TLs.

articleTitle: Ionograms Scaling by Using the Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Ionosphere in F layer has the most irregularity for phenomenon occurrence of amplitude scintillation which leads to the problem in the satellite signals. Ionosphere can be observed by Ionosonde to study F2 layer critical frequency (foF2) parameter and height of F layer (h'F) parameter from the ionogram. This paper presents the convolutional neural network (CNN) to determine foF2 and h'F parameters. The simulation start from passing the ionogram images to the proposed CNN model with 2,000 epoch training. The simulated accuracies of both foF2 and h'F parameters are equal to 92.8% and 98.4%, respectively.

articleTitle: The Maximum Power Point Tracking of Charging Stations by using an Adaptive Incremental Conductance
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive incremental conductance to track the maximum power point for charging station. The proposed technique is used to increase the performance of the conventional incremental conductance approach. The simulation results via MATLAB/SimPowerSystem<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> are used for validation. The results show that the MPP of PV panel can be achieved even the irradiance value is changed instantaneously. Moreover, the proposed adaptive step-size of duty cycle is very simple for proposed implementation.

articleTitle: Development of Bi-Directional Portable People Counter System based IoT
abstract: This paper proposes a portable system to count the number of people entering and exiting a space. The system is developed for use in locations which have only one entrance/exit. The system detects people who walk through the door, calculates the number people, and sends the data to the Blynk and Line Notify servers which forwards the information to a user’s smartphone. To make the system standalone and reduce WiFi connection problems, the GSM cellular data network has been selected to communicate with the Blynk and Line Notify servers. The average accuracy of counting people using the proposed system, is approximately 97.33%.

articleTitle: Improvement of Isolation with EBG Wall Applied by E Model Structure for IEEE 802.11b/g/n
abstract: This paper presents the improvement of the isolation wall with the Electromagnetic Bandgap E-model (EBG-E) structure isolating between two rectangular patches. The EBG-E structure with 2x8 elements of the unit cell operates at a frequency of 2.45 GHz and achieves the antenna's mutual coupling of 13dB. Also, the peak gain of radiation patterns of the proposed antenna shift slily 15 degrees while the black lobe can be reduced lower than 10 dB compared to the antenna without the EBG-E model approximately.

articleTitle: Signal Prediction of a GPR System Mounted on Drone by Using Ray-Tracing Technique
abstract: Signal prediction of time-domain (TD) ground-penetrating radar (GPR) installed on drone by employing the ray-tracing technique is proposed. This work employs the TD uniform geometrical theory of diffraction (UTD) method including the geometrical optic (GO) rays tracing technique to find the GPR reflected signal from the ground layer and the underground object. Moreover, the diffracted ray path of a monostatic GPR is also calculated. The fast Fourier transforms (FFT) method is employed to find the TD-GPR signal. Three-dimensional (3D) locations of a drone are taken into account. The calculated results found that the proposed procedure can be used to predict the GPR mounted on a drone signal. The reflected GPR signal of the ground is very strong. The reflected GPR signal of an underground object can be calculated. However, the signal strength is very weak. In future work, the study of the position error of a drone trajectory will be presented.

Author Keywords: Time domain (TD) uniform geometrical theory of diffraction (UTD)

articleTitle: Design of 5.5 GHz Band Notching for Printed UWB Pentagonal Monopole Antenna
abstract: This paper proposes three techniques band notching of 5.5 GHz for the printed UWB pentagonal monopole antenna. By embedding narrow slits including the inverted C-shaped and inverted open- end triangle-shaped into the patch of monopole antenna, frequency band rejection of 5.5 GHz is achieved. Another technique, by placing small strip in rectangle shape embedded in CPW central feed line, frequency rejection is obtained. The measurement S11 results of the proposed antennas show the frequency coverage of 3.1-10.6 GHz with frequency rejection from 5.2 to 5.8 GHz. All proposed antennas show radiation patterns with nearly omni-directional in xz plane and likely bi-directional in yz plane. The maximum gain of 4.5 dBi is reached at 7.5 GHz and minimum gain of −0.89 dBi at 5.5 GHz are also obtained. It is obviously that the proposed antennas show potential to reduce electromagnetic interferences at 5.5 GHz band, therefore they are suitable for various UWB applications.

articleTitle: A Design of Heat Sink for Lithium-ion Battery Pack
abstract: In this paper, all of us focus on design heat sink size that suitable for the battery pack to dissipate heat from the battery into the surrounding air. First calculating battery internal temperature for design heat sink size. After that simulation batteries to observe battery temperature when applying heat sink in addition to not apply heat sink. Finally, the experiment shows the simulation results in case of the applied heat sink on the battery pack currently am able to decreasing battery temperature.

articleTitle: Dual-Bands Operation base on an Asymmetrical Double Triangular Slot Fed by CPW with stair-step for WLAN 2.45 GHz and 5.5 GHz
abstract: This paper presents a dual bands antenna with an asymmetrical double triangular slot fed by a coplanar waveguide (CPW) strip for WLAN 2.45 GHz and 5.5 GHz. The double triangular slot can respond to dual bands. Moreover, a stair-step-impedance matching technique was applied for improving impedance matching at higher band operation. It is placed on the inductive coupling point. The presented antenna having an input impedance of 50 ohms was fabricated on a FR-4 substrate. The results were in good agreement. The antenna's reflection coefficients (S11) less than 10 dB are found at 2.12 - 2.64 GHz and 4.7 - 6.83 GHz. Therefore, it can be concluded that this antenna can use at 2.45 GHz, 5.2 GHz, and 5.8 GHz of WLAN communication.

articleTitle: Automatic Chord Recognition Technique for a Music Visualizer Application
abstract: Stage lighting is a powerful tool to draw the audience into the music engagement in any music or concert performances. The traditional stage lighting control often requires professional operators and lots of time-consuming preparations. This paper presents an automatic chord recognition technique for a music visualizer application. The proposed technique is based on chroma vector and chord template fitting algorithms. The detected chord can apply to control the proper light color on stage for audience best experience. The experiments done by utilizing the GarageBand software application to mimic a variety of musical instruments, a microchip microcontroller performs signal processing function, and the detected chord displays on a LCD. Experiment results have indicated that our proposed algorithm can accurately detect chords for all instruments and in both major and minor chords. This algorithm presents a simple and ease of use design since it does not require complicate machine learning or statistical process techniques. However, there are few detection errors appear in complex chords due to hardware limitation deployed in the experiment and the algorithm needs an improvement.

articleTitle: Adaptive Control for Nonlinear Processes
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel mechanism to achieve an advanced adaptive controller for nonlinear processes. The combination between unfalsified control theory and artificial intelligence is demonstrated via an application of a pH neutralization process. The selling point of this approach is how to create an adaptive controller set that handles a change of set-points. Finally, a simple PID controller structure is used to show how the algorithm works in practice.

articleTitle: An Improved Quantization Algorithm For Electric Power Inspection
abstract: Along with the rapid development of deep learning and artificial intelligence technology, machine vision instead of human vision is used in many applications, such as defect detection, face recognition, etc. In the power system, it is very important to use computer vision algorithms to perform intelligent defect detection on images taken by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles, robots and other equipment. Traditional image compression algorithms aim to reduce the pixel distortion based on the visual characteristics of the human eye, which are not suitable for machine vision. Considering the limited communication channel bandwidth, the images generally compressed at low bitrate. Then, the blocking artifact introduced by compression will result in undetectable or false detection of the state of small electrical components, such as insulator strings, anti-vibration hammers, etc. In this paper, a quantization algorithm which is oriented to machine vision is proposed to address these problems. First of all, low-level image features are extracted based on CNN network. Subsequently, according to the extracted features, the original images are divided into key areas and non-key areas. Finally, key areas are encoded with smaller quantization level and non-key areas are encoded with lager quantization level. Experimental results demonstrate that compared with traditional image compression algorithm, the proposed algorithm improves the accuracy of defect detection from 20% to more than 80% at bitrate of 0.24bpp.

articleTitle: Harmonic Suppression by Using Input and Output L-shaped Microstrip Lines For Dual-mode Resonator Filter Applications
abstract: This paper proposed a harmonic suppression using input and output coupled feed-lines for dual-mode resonator filter applications. The folded coupled feed-lines are coupled in the form of the L-shaped input and output feeders to the dual-mode resonator. Two opened-end feed-lines are added to enhance the upper stopband performances. The dual-mode resonator operates at 1.95 GHz, which is found that an insertion loss is less than 0.6 dB and a return loss is better than 25 dB. A proper tuning length for the input/output feed results in a high rejection level which a signal suppression is better than 20 dB over a frequency band from 2.2 GHz to 4.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Circular Patch with Symmetric Strips Antenna for 5G Applications
abstract: In this research, a circular patch antenna encircled by wide-circular-slot incorporated with symmetric strips is designed to operate over the middle-band of 5G applications. This proposed antenna is constructed of a copper and glazed on FR4 substrate with ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> of 4.3 and height of 1.6 mm. It is fed by a 50-ohms coplanar waveguide, which printed on a same side of the radiating circular patch. Obviously, it exhibits a bidirectional pattern with 10 dB return loss, minimum and maximum gains of 1.76 dBi, and 5.64 dBi, respectively covered 2-6 GHz. All appropriated parameters have been carried out by using an electromagnetic simulation tool. To evaluate its suitability in 5G applications, numerical results will be investigated and analyzed.

articleTitle: 5GNR : The Suitable Communication Technology for V2X in Thailand Vehicular Environment
abstract: Nowadays, vehicular communication is a famous technology. This technology increases the efficiency of vehicle and road safety. IEEE 802.11p and LTE-V are introduced for more vehicle safety. 3GPP defined a new technology (5GNR V2X) for new service of communication between vehicles, in Thailand is still not explicit in which technology is suitable. This work proposes a comparison of vehicle to vehicle (V2V) communication link performance in terms of Packet Error Rate (PER) versus Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) and PER versus distance between vehicle in various environments. Simulation processes are created according to communication standards such as doppler shift, path delay and path gain. Our results show that 5GNR V2X is proper technology for communication link between vehicles in Thailand. 5GNR V2X is the highest performance according to PER values.

articleTitle: Quadrature Sinusoidal Oscillator with Grounded Resistors and Capacitors Using VDCCs
abstract: This paper presents the quadrature oscillator using voltage differencing current conveyors (VDCCs) - based on the LC circuit parallel to the positive and negative resistors. In this design, two active devices, VDCC is constructed with two grounded capacitors and three grounded resistors. The sine waves are obtained both voltage and current mode. It can generate quadrature sinusoidal voltage output and two current outputs with amplitude controllability. Two current outputs with high impedance are180ºdegree phase difference are also obtained. Adjusting the condition and frequency of signal generation can be done independently via electronic feature. The total harmonic distortion is less than 0.97 % and power consumption at a maximum frequency of 1.12MHz is 1.82mW at power supply voltages ±0.9 V. The workability of the circuit is verified by PSPICE.

articleTitle: Integration of Solar and Wind Power Sources in Power Grid with Energy Storage System using Discrete Balancing
abstract: This paper presents the power grid system analysis with solar power sources, wind turbine resources, and energy storage system integration by using the Open Distribution System Simulator (OpenDSS) program. According to the energy storage systems (ESS), improve grid reliability, flexibility, and energy quality issues of renewable energy sources. This study analyzes the power grid system and its continuity when the solar power sources and wind turbine resources have worked with energy storage systems. The OpenDSS is selected to represent the performance of the proposed study in this article. The simulation results found that the integration of photovoltaic, Wind Turbine Power energy, and energy storage systems can decrease the minimum power consumption and power loss.

articleTitle: Design of Optimal PIλDµAν Controller for Temperature Process Control System by Flower Pollination Algorithm
abstract: This paper describes the design of a PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">µ</sup>A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ν</sup> controller for the temperature process control system by using the flower pollination algorithm (FPA). The PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">µ</sup>A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ν</sup> controller is expressed by a PIDA controller which their integral and derivative orders are presented by fractional numbers, leading to more tuning parameters. The PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">µ</sup>A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ν</sup> controller design is applied to the constrained optimization problem which can be stated as the objective function and inequality constraints. Optimal seven parameters of the PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">µ</sup>A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ν</sup> controller are sought by using the FPA to minimize the objective function under inequality constraints in search space. As simulation results, the PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">µ</sup>A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ν</sup> controller designed by the FPA provides better performance than PID and PIDA controllers in both set-point tracking and disturbance regulating in the feedback control loop of the temperature process control system.

articleTitle: Quantization of Impedance Stability in Frequency Domain
abstract: A method based on Sample Standard Deviation (SSD) is suggested here to quantify impedance stability in frequency domain. Firstly, impedance instability factor, δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>, is introduced as an indicator of that could be used for impedance stability quantifications of measured or simulated impedance data of Radio Frequency (RF) and high-power devices. The method is used then for a generic real/imaginary impedance trajectory as an example to clarify calculation process. Finally, the introduced approach has been used to quantify impedance stabilities in some RF devices such as stable impedance antenna of 5G in-band full duplex (IBFD) transceivers, microstrip low-pass filter and hybrid coupler. Also, suitable efficiency of the method to follow up correct design direction to smoothen impedance of an antenna is realized.

articleTitle: Optical Checksum in Multi Tunnels for High Speed Error Detection using Ring Resonator System
abstract: A novel optical checksum high speed approach for error detection is proposed for use in a multi tunnel wavelength domain. By using this technique, all processes were performed by passing light through optical hardware (PANDA ring resonator together with add/drop filter). Outputs achieved from dynamic states utilizing the bright-dark soliton conversion control was utilized to secure the optical checksum creation process. The add/drop filter was utilized as an essential device in the proposed system. The results proved that the proposed design could achieve optical checksum in wavelength domain for real time error detection. This method could also quickly create and check the accuracy of information using optical processes. The wavelength of the multi tunnels must be within 50% of the center wavelength of the input signal system to maintain data integrity for optical communication.

articleTitle: Recursive Least Squares based Seizure Detection of Epileptic EEG signals
abstract: In this research paper, multiresolutional recursive least squares (RLS) method is proposed for the automatic epileptic seizure identification present in the electroencephalogram (EEG) signals and detection is performed using relative band power feature map. The main aim of this method is to improve the seizure classification accuracy of the epileptic EEG signals. In the proposed RLS based approach, initially the EEG signal is pre-processed using RLS dependent adaptive filter followed by the segment-wise computation of the relative band power in terms of frequency present in the epileptic seizure information. At last, support vector machine (SVM) is used to classify the EEG signal into seizure and non-seizure data. The experimental investigation shows that the RLS approach has attained a classification accuracy of 94.876%, 97.594% sensitivity, and 91.856% specificity. The proposed scheme has proven to be significant for EEG seizure detection, which will support doctors in the epileptic detection.

articleTitle: Comparison of Figure of Merit of Different Circular Coil Used in Inductive Power Transfer System
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of figure of merit (FOM) of circular coil used in the inductive power transfer (IPT) system. Four transmitter coils with different physical dimension are compared. Key parameters, including inner diameter, outer diameter, and number of turns of the coil are considered. Magnetic coupling coefficient, output power, and system efficiency obtained from each coil are determined by the experimental measurement. Total length of the litz-wire and pad area required from each coil is also evaluated. The comparison results of FOM reported in this work can be used as the design guideline for the IPT coil.

articleTitle: Converting a q-ary Symmetric Channel into an Error-Erasure Channel with Erasure Marking
abstract: The ability to mark erasure precisely is useful for data communications. The concept of error locating vector of Vector Symbol Decoding (VSD) has been used to mark error positions. This paper proposes the idea of converting none or some errors to erasures to reduce the decoding complexity. If the number of erroneous symbols input to VSD is limited to x, the number of matrix inversion of sized x will increase. However, all matrix inversions of larger size are eliminated. The q-ary Symmetric Channel is selected for packet-based transmission. Densities of parity check patterns are investigated, and results show that lower density of 1’s provides better performance. In terms of code word length, shorter code word is preferred as it requires less overhead.

articleTitle: Power and Performance Evaluation of Optimized NP-domino Comparator in 7nm FinFET for TLBs
abstract: Domino-based address comparators are used in Translation look aside buffers (TLB) and are a part of address translation in microprocessors. NFET pull-down logic with precharge based domino comparators are used in Translation Lookaside Buffers (TLB) in general to achieve higher speeds. Due to technology scaling, the resistance and capacitance due to metal routing are higher. The NFET pull-down logic with precharge based domino comparators should be optimized to meet the power and performance requirements. However, in the advanced nodes, the NFET and PFET electrical parameters such as mobility are almost similar. We explore the advantages of using a PFET pull-up logic with discharge-based domino comparator. In this paper, we propose a banking technique using PFET pull-up logic with a discharge-based domino comparator. This technique was implemented for 32-bit, 64-bit, and 128-bit address comparison.

articleTitle: A Semi-supervised Method of Non-intrusive Load Monitoring with Answer-Question Technique
abstract: Nowadays, there is not an easy-to-implement system to help residential customers in monitoring and displaying electricity consumption because such a system needs installation of measuring instruments at every interested electric appliance. This difficulty can be overcome by one point or Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM). This paper presents a semi-supervised method of NILM with the answer-question technique. The proposed method uses selected machine learning techniques for clustering electricity consumption of various electric appliances. In particular, an improved K-Means technique with optimal number of cluster determination and feature selection methods is presented. Moreover, an answer-question technique is employed to improve clustering results. Subsequently, some experimental results are given to show effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method. Consequently, the proposed method can help in uncovering details of electricity, meanwhile reducing cost of installing measuring instruments.

articleTitle: Fractional-Order System Identification of Temperature Process Rig Control System using Flower Pollination Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a fractional-order system identification of a temperature process rig control by a flower pollination algorithm (FPA). The fractional-order model provides more accuracy than the integer-order model by the concept of fractional calculus. The identification of fractional-order model is applied via the modern optimization problem. The objective function of the optimization problem is considered as the sum-absolute error (SAE) between the actual temperature of the process plant and the temperature of the candidate fractional-order model. The FPA, one of the most efficient metahueristis optimization methods, attempts to search the optimal parameters of a fractional-order model for minimizing the objective function in search space. As results, the proposed model of temperature process rig control plant can give a higher accuracy than the traditional model.

articleTitle: Right Angle Slot Fabric Antenna for Wireless Body Area Network
abstract: This paper is presenting a right-angle slot fabric antenna for the Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) and dual-band. This technique uses different slot sizes in different positions appropriately. The right-angle slot fabric antenna consisting of a right-angle slot, and two smaller right-angle slots are applied to produce Circular Polarize (CP) resonance of high band. The paper is presenting an analysis of right angle microstrip slot antenna to attain dual-frequency, achieving slant ±45° linear polarization. The proposed right-angle slot fabric antenna uses the 2.4 GHz and 5.2 GHz band as a transmitting antenna of the wireless body area network. The prototype of a simulated antenna is fabricated and experimentally as well. The measured results were shown to be reasonable for the simulated ones. Moreover, the peak gains of the antenna is approximate 5.2 dBi at 2.4 GHz and 5.5 dBi at 5.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Development of Multi-Purpose Donation Box based on the Internet of Things
abstract: This paper proposes a multipurpose donation box system. The system is developed to reduce fraud. The system counts the number of coins and bills inserted into the donation box, calculates the total amount of money specified for each purpose, and sends the data to the Blynk server, which forwards the information to the owner's smartphone. To make the system standalone and reduce WiFi connection problems, the GSM cellular data network has been selected to communicate with the Blynk server. The accuracy of computing the value of inserted money is 100%, and the average total acceptance rate of both coins and bills is around 91.29%.

articleTitle: Modern Men’s Shirts-Fitting Robot Using DC Servo Motor with Fuzzy-PI Control via on Cloud-based System
abstract: The modern men's shirts-fitting robot is controlled with fuzzy plus proportional plus integral controller called as F-PI via on cloud-based communication presented here with an effective cost value add of high-end superstore especially for modern shop-dressing room services. Now, the customer's life styles have been change caused by COVID-19 situations which they must be kept the social distancing all time. The both of RFID and QR code technique are used for creating a unique code of any men shirt products in the databased server of a system and also the way to access to use the men's shirts-fitting robot with an efficiency time management scheme. The user's body size information's such as the shoulder, neck, chest or waistline are need as necessary data to operate the robot system. The small of DC servo motors (DCSMs) are driven by fuzzy-PI controller which is used for resizing the robot's body size that is related to the real user's body size. For unknown or non-linear of mathematical model of robot body load, the F-PI controller is the way to solve this problem with high performance enough, but the suitable tuning parameters are required. The room experimental results are shown that the overall system can work well as design concept, but in the real on-site shop it must be improved for more accuracy and practical to use. As a result, the customers and service persons can change their new normal behaviors for improving their online shopping with social distancing scheme with more efficiency, comfortable, up-to-date and safety life.

articleTitle: Electronically Tunable Quadrature Sinusoidal Oscillator Using VDDDAs
abstract: This research proposes the sinusoidal oscillator that can provide two sine waves with 90° degree phase shift. The proposed oscillator is derived from lossy and lossless integrator circuits. The proposed quadrature sinusoidal oscillator uses one resistor, two grounded capacitors and two active elements, called voltage differencing differential difference amplifier (VDDDA). By adding additional two resistors, the voltage magnitude of a sinusoidal signal is controllable with low impedance output voltage node. The frequency of the generated sine wave and the condition of oscillation is orthogonally adjusted. In addition, the condition of the signal generator can be adjusted electronically. The performance of the presented sine wave generator has been validated through Pspice simulation. The active element, VDDDA is implemented from two commercial ICs, LM13700 and AD830.

articleTitle: Thickness Measurement of Double Layer Transparent Material Using Triangular Path Cyclic Interferometer
abstract: The new scheme of a non-contact thickness measurement of multi-layer thin films with improving the sensitivity, accuracy, and performance of the measurement techniques is reported in this paper. Single- and double-layer film thickness measurement using different polarization states were studied. An alternative architecture using triangular cyclic interferometer with simultaneous measurements of reference and sample arms by splitting the beam at the output of interferometer is mathematically achieved. The polarization phase shift using two steps algorithm is observed, with steps shift of n/2 rad for a double layer sample. This shows that the polarization state has an impact on the thickness measurement of different thin- film materials.

articleTitle: Development of Electric Door Control System using MRS Developers Studio for Low-floor Bus
abstract: This research aimed to develop and improve the passenger gate from a pneumatic system to an electrical system as a guideline for use in the automotive industry. Used MRS Developers Studio to write the programs to control the door system and motor control. Relied on data transmission with CAN, which is a standard used in the automotive industry worldwide and based on the J1939 standard. The simulated doors that created can be used to enhance the safety mechanisms and comply with the 2014 announcement by the Department of Land Transport regarding gates and emergency gates used on vehicles that transport passengers.

articleTitle: A Simple Glide Slope Transmitter for Navigation Aids System Education
abstract: The purpose of article is to develop a simple glide slope transmitter for navigation aids systems for applying to teaching in avionics engineering and related fields. The glide slope transmitter developed in connection to the Digital RF signal generator, can be used to test the onboard glide slope receiver. The implemented results shown that a simple glide slope transmitter developed using a transmit power of 1 mW can transmit radio waves to the glide slope receiver at transmission distance of approximately 5 m. The advantage of developed transmitter is flexible in modify various parameters and measure the transmitter radio waveform with theoretical quality of aircraft communication system and easy to construct and implement in a practical laboratory and the hangar for testing the glide slope receiver on aircraft as convenient.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of an 18 MW Wind Farm in Nakhon Ratchasima Province
abstract: This paper presents a performance analysis of an onshore wind farm in Thepharak district, Nakhon Ratchasima province, Thailand. There are 2 wind farms in the area, each wind farm consists of 3 MW Vestas V136 wind turbines in a total of 30 wind turbines. There are totally 60 wind turbines with capacity of 180 MW. The paper considered only 1 feeder with 6 wind turbines with total capacity of 18MW. The data measurement used the SCADA system for collecting parameters that are composed machine availability, grid availability, system availability, and energy production. The measured data had been collected for one year during January to December 2019. The capacity factor was therefore calculated from the measured data. The annual capacity factor of wind turbine was found to be 38.82% and the total energy production was 64.9865 GWh.

articleTitle: Modeling of Electric Field Enhancement by Various Defects in Insulation of a High Voltage Cable
abstract: This paper presents the modeling and simulation of a defect in cable insulation, where the electric field enhancement at this local site might lead to the progressive deterioration until upcoming failure of a high voltage (HV) cable prior to its design life expectancy. The simulation results highlight the electric field enhancement of physical models by occurring various defects embedded in polymeric cable insulation layer in the cases of a protrusion, a single void and two voids using the Finite Element Analysis (FEA) technique.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Multi-Parent and Single Parent Selection of RPL for Smart Grid
abstract: To support the number of low-power devices of AMI network, RPL protocol is one of the most interested protocol to be implemented for the limited ability and energy resource devices. Parent selection is the critical function which is used to select the node to forward data from meters to the utility. The tradeoff between energy consumption and PDR is the major issue of parent selection that is difficult to be addressed by the single parent scheme. Therefore, multi-parent schemes are proposed to solve this issue by splitting the large size of data into small packets and forward them to all candidate parents considered by parents' quality. In this paper, we investigate the optimal parameters for two efficient multi-parent selection including MELT and MAHP. Then, we compare their performance to the single parent scheme and analyze their advantages/disadvantages. As a result, a single parent gives the highest network lifetime since it consumes less energy for forwarding data but it cannot balance meter workload. Moreover, it cannot achieve the high PDR at long transmission distance. On the other hand, MELT and MAHP achieves higher PDR with long distance and can balance workload effectively which can facilitate the maintenance planning. However, they present lower network lifetime as compared to single parent.

articleTitle: The PLR Recovery for GMR/TMR Devices Using Internal Thermal Heat and External Magnetizing
abstract: A pinned layer reversal failure in GMR or TMR devices could be recovered using internal thermal energy and external magnetization. The thermal energy from the dynamic flying height control heater activates the exchange layer to an unstable state. Its magnetic domain could be oriented freely. Then, the external magnetic field realigns the magnetic domain of the exchange layer to the right orientation that provides the proper magnetization of the pinned layer. This recovery is helpful to correct the head defect and enhances its reliability.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Low-Loss Impedance Transformers Using Bi-Characteristic Impedance Transmission Lines (BCITLs)
abstract: This paper presents a new miniaturization technique of impedance transformers using the bi-characteristic-impedance transmission lines (BCITLs). The asymmetric compact microstrip resonant cell (CMRC) is employed to implement BCITLs, and is optimized based on its ABCD parameters to obtain desired impedance transformers. It is found that the asymmetric CMRC physical length is 50 % of that of the conventional quarter-wave transformer (QWT) (50 % physical size reduction) operating at 922.5 MHz with acceptable bandwidth and return loss.

articleTitle: E-Payment and It’s Effects on Cash in Thailand
abstract: Thailand has experienced high growth in e-payment as the government and industries introduce digital payment services as alternatives to cash payment. This paper aims to study e-payment effects on cash by constructing models to forecast value and analyze the structural change of e-payment and cash time series data. The data are a time series of monthly currency in circulation or cash data from January 2005 to September 2019 and e-payment data from January 2010 to March 2019. Using decomposition of components, Holt-Winters' additive method (HW), and ARIMA model, results demonstrate that e-payment is growing because it has an upward trend component. In terms of cash data, it grows upward initially and then continually has a downward trend. The implication is that e-payment growth has affected cash growth while cash is still growing with a decreasing rate. The forecasting models and implications discovered are grounds for conducting further investigations and crafting related policies in the future.

articleTitle: Active Vibration Control of Three-Floor Structure System under Seismic Excitation based on Fixed Structure PID Controller Tuning by H∞ Synthesis
abstract: Designing a structural control system to suppress unexpected disturbance in the tall building under seismic excitation is very challenging. To achieve an Active Vibration Control (AVC) goal, Active Mass Damping (AMD) systems have been implemented in modern architectures. However, it is difficult to tune the control parameters to achieve good performance and efficiency. In this paper, a fixed-structure H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> control method is proposed to tune PID gains for the AMD system in a three-floor scale model under Loma Prieta Earthquake excitation. The results show the efficiency of the proposed method. Under seismic excitation, the AMD system with the fixed-structure H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> control can significantly reduce the maximum deflection of the third floor compared with the AMD system controlled by PID-PSO tuner and without the AMD system.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modelling of a Sensorless Singly Fed Induction Machine with Rotor Flux Oriented Control
abstract: This investigation forms the preliminary work leading to the study of a Sensorless Singly Fed Induction Machine (SFIM). The paper presents an investigation made on the Singly Fed Induction Machine and its behaviour under dynamic and steady-state conditions. A vector controlled PWM converter is connected to the stator side of the machine. To produce flux and torque, the stator current is controlled using a rotor-flux-oriented reference frame. Matlab/Simulink was used for the simulation of the vector control system of an induction machine. The simulation results show that the flux and torque can be regulated independently to match the reference signals. Moreover, a comparison of simulation and calculation results in a steady-state condition shows a good agreement.

articleTitle: Smart Solar Cell e-Warning Signs Board via on Cloud-based Control for Social Distancing Alert
abstract: In this paper, the visualization LED board was designed and implemented called as solar cell e-warning sign board which can generate the digital data field commands for the variable texts, messages or warning sign symbols as on demand or automatically display change in order to input change via on cloud communication in a long distance control served for the social distancing methodology in a new normal of COVID-19 situations. An e-warning sign board run on digital communication command with Arduino controllers based and cloud control plus GPS tracking which can served an important information on demand request of crowd user's area such as food court, restaurant or public transportation stations which must be manage for social distancing policy. However, e-warning sign board may be the different sizes and shape according to the natural scenes and the crowd area size and it has to display the variable message in real-time situations both for day and night time. And about its energy consumption, solar energy is a clean and renewable power resource, for non-storability in a standalone photovoltaic (PV) system can be mitigated by incorporating energy storage devices like battery to store the electrical energy produced by solar panel when the sun is shining and to supply power when the sun is not shining. Batteries are one of the critical component in the standalone PV system and always preventive maintenance for more reliability of use with a long time. So, this paper present a low cost e-warning sign board with cloud control plus GPS that can also improve the system performance for a long distance access control, Arduino controller based and PV battery charging system. As a result, the customers and service persons can change their new normal behaviors for improving their social distancing usage with more an efficiency, comfortable, up-to-date and safety in present day.

articleTitle: Design of Reactance-to-Reactance Transformers in Single Stub Tuning
abstract: The reactance-to-reactance transformer (RRT) technique is proposed in this paper for applying in the tuning circuit to miniaturize the tuning stub. These associated RRT formulas are derived based on conjugately characteristic-impedance transmission line (CCITL) equations and the ABCD parameters. The proposed RRT analytical formulas are applied to both short- and open-circuit tuning stubs. Then, the physical length, electrical length and reflection coefficient are observed at the operating frequency of 2.4 GHz. Simulation results prove that the proposed RRTs can be applied to shorten the tuning stub length compared to that of the conventional single stub tuning.

articleTitle: Detection of 2,4,6-Trinitrotoluene by MIP-composite Based Electrochemical Sensor
abstract: In Thailand, there are terrorist groups active in some areas where casualties from their operations are civilians. Most of these casualties are from explosive device. The main component of the device is high explosive compound called 2,4,6-trinitrotoluene (TNT). Detection of TNT from objects and places in the suspected or area bombardment will provide useful evidence for the authority. In this work, we fabricate an electrochemical TNT sensor based on molecularly imprinted polymers (MIP) nanocomposites. The sensor aimed at TNT trace detection from solution of solid specimens. The sensor was able to detect TNT in solution with 3 log-scale linearity with 0.4 ppt lower limit of detection. The selectivity of the sensor toward TNT was considerably high compared with the other nitro compound.

articleTitle: A Development of a Wrist-Worn Fall Detection using Binary Neural Network
abstract: This paper presents a development of wrist-worn device for fall detection which can be a fall detector and localizer. The system consists of a wristband and a mobile phone. The wristband acts as a fall detector and the mobile phone acts as an IoT gateway for locating and transmitting the fall information to the people involved. The fall detection method is based on a threshold-based and a binary neural network that uses to reduce resources and computational requirements. Experimental results showed that the accuracy of the proposed method was 97.23%. However, for some movement patterns such as hand clapping or hand waving, the system might be given a low accuracy.

articleTitle: Wide-Angle Dual-Band Absorber Based on Nanowire-Hyperbolic Medium
abstract: We proposed a dual-band absorber in the visible regime by using nanowire-hyperbolic medium, which is composed of an array of subwavelength-sized hybrid nanowires immersed in dielectric matrix, as a top layer, silicon dioxide as a middle layer, and gold as a bottom layer. Each nanowire is made by core-shell structure, which has silicon as a core and gold as a shell. We found that the dual-band absorption originated from impedance matching between incident medium impedance and input impedance of the proposed absorber at first- and second-order resonant modes. Furthermore, the absorbance can be controlled by adding or reducing filling factor of hyperbolic medium layer. In addition, the absorption performance of the absorber retains well in wide angles. This dual-band absorber is a good candidate for potential applications such as thermal radiation tailoring and sensitive detection.

articleTitle: Channel Estimation based Pilot Signal with BS Identification Code for LTE-TDD Massive MIMO Downlink systems
abstract: This paper presents a technique to use an orthogonality property of Hadamard code for reducing the impact of pilot contamination in LTE-TDD Massive MIMO systems. Pilot signal is modulated with Hadamard code to identify base station in cellular network. The low computational complexity suboptimal linear LS criterion is applied to estimate channel state information at base station and mitigates the effect of pilot contamination in case of full pilot reuse in multi-cell scenarios. Numerical results show that SINR performance and achievable downlink rate obtained from the proposed technique are higher than that of the LS conventional algorithm in aspect of time-varying fading channel and high cross gain of pilot power from adjacent cells.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of LTE Advanced System with CoMP DPS under Hotspot Scenarios
abstract: Number of mobile devices are increasing and traffic demand of using mobile data services has been growing extremely with the trend of this generation. To improve system performance to support increasing demand in the future networks, 5G mobile communication systems based on LTE Advanced (LTE-A) technology were introduced. Users’ experienced throughput has been one of the important goals in 5G systems that can be achievable by improving the cell edge performance. Coordinated Multipoint (CoMP) was considered for managing inter-cell interference at cell-edge in particular a Dynamic Point Selection (DPS), a mechanism to provide cell load balancing and interference mitigation in the Network. In DPS, Transmission Point (TP) of User Equipment (UE) will be switched dynamically among the cooperating set of TPs. Several DPS mechanisms have been proposed to date, however the performance of DPS in hotspot scenarios has not been studied. In this paper, the LTE-A system performance based on the implementation of DPS with different CoMP clustering patterns under hotspot scenarios is evaluated. The system level simulation has been used with non-full buffered video streaming traffic model for realistic scenarios. The simulation results show the system performance in terms of the peak throughput, the average throughput and the cell-edge throughput of the system with the CoMP DPS implementation. Finally, the DPS performance gains obtained in such scenarios are presented.

articleTitle: Face Recognition Based on Fusion of Zonal Images
abstract: Partial face recognition from videos has practical applications to surveillance and threats monitoring, but is difficult to perform accurately due to an absence of facial information and due to environmental effects, such as a poor resolution, noise, blur, and variation in light-intensity, in the input images. This research aims to design a method for partial face recognition based on a technique called zonal-image fusion. The proposed method uses different pose images from two videos as a source and recognizes the images against frontal faces in a database. The method handles misalignment and the absence of facial information in input images by fusing the input images and arriving at a single combined image. The fused image is partition into 3 × 3 sub-blocks. We compare each sub-block in the fused image to the corresponding sub-block in a database image, to obtain a measure of similarity. The database image that is most similar to the fused image is taken to an output image from face recognition. We compare the proposed method to existing methods by using publicly available dataset. The comparison shows that the proposed method is promising, although the face recognition rates have an enormous room for improvement.

articleTitle: A Study on Memristor Based Mo/n-Si/Mo Schottky Diode with Wide Electrodes
abstract: This research purposed on a semiconductor device with two-terminal electrodes to demonstrate on the memristive device following the fabrication processed. The Molybdenum(Mo) thin-film deposited onto an n-type silicon wafer of resistivity 40-50 Ω-cm by E-beam evaporation. The planar MSM Schottky diode having a widely-separated electrode structure. The equivalent circuit has been consisting of two diodes, two resistors, memristor device is proposed to 2D2R structures. There is a relationship between magnetic flux and electric charge. Furthermore, in the direct and alternating current tests, there is a decrease and increase of current. In addition to changes in current-voltage, those show the behavior of the typical pinched Hysteresis loops memristive. As described, the result of current-voltage is dependent on the frequency and the input voltage level, which is the state of a set and reset. According to the time domain are represents the nature of the memory status.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Noise Cancellation Based for a BFSK Demodulation in a Narrow Band Communication
abstract: Another scheme of a binary frequency phase shift keying (BFSK) signal demodulation has been presented in this paper. The proposed demodulated scheme utilizes an ANC-based adaptive signal processing. The adaptive algorithm which adapts the coefficients of the ANC system will be constrained in adaptation sequence corresponding to each symbol interval of the received BFSK signal. By using this scheme, the system will provide demodulated behavior similar to an integrated and dump correlator of an optimum receiver. The analytical and simulation results have shown that the proposed system can demodulate the received BFSK signal in AWGN channel. Furthermore, the system provides the same performance as the optimum receiver.

articleTitle: Study of K-Band Rectifiers with Different Topologies
abstract: This paper focuses on study of different millimeter-wave rectifier topologies which are fundamental matching without harmonic termination, with harmonic termination and with inductive matching. The rectifiers are designed and fabricated with low-cost commercial Schottky diodes. Measured conversion efficiency is 25.08% without harmonic-termination, 26.2% with harmonic-termination and 30.08% with inductive matching topology. The experiment shows that the inductive matching provides the highest efficiency compared to other topologies. It proves that inductive matching is suitable for high frequency rectifier design with lossy substrates.

articleTitle: Applied Switching Bilateral Filter for Color Images under Mixed Noise
abstract: In the image, mixed noise color images independently contaminate each component of the color image with varying strength. In this paper, we propose a detection switching bilateral filter (DSBF) to reduce the mixed noise for the color images. We compare the performance of the proposed filter with three well-known filters including SBF, BM3D, and NCSR. We improve the performance of the SBF filter for color images by enhancing the noise separation process based on primary color values. In simulation results, the DSBF maintains high performance for color images than others. On the other hand, the performance filter-based non-iterative scheme, SBF and BM3D, significantly decrease for color images since the quality of output in each component cannot maintain the filter performance.

articleTitle: Semi-Adaptive, Reliability Oriented EH-WSN Energy Management Algorithm
abstract: The deployment of Wireless Sensor Nodes which often deploy in large number, are required to be self-sustainable by utilizing Energy Harvesters for harvesting ambient energy as the node's power source. Several energy managements schemes have been proposed, dealing with the intermittent power generation problem introduced by the harvester. However, reliability and transmission consistency of the node are not their primary concern. This study proposes an Energy harvesting powered Wireless Sensor node energy management algorithm which balances between transmitting data with desired interval and providing sensor network reliability by transmitting the nodes status in low harvesting rate. The simulation results show that, with the proposed algorithm the node is able to provide an average 15 second interval data transmission under fluctuating harvesting rate, verified their status periodically and also gives more consistency in data acquisition which is necessary in monitoring application.

articleTitle: Current Driven Asymmetrical Series Resonant Converter
abstract: This paper presents analysis, design and simulation of current driven asymmetrical series resonant converter. The state-plane diagram approach was used for the analysis. It can be shown that the analytical results obtained from this approach are very precise. The control characteristics are also obtained from the analysis, and are used for the converter design. The analysis also shows that the proposed converter has the property of zero current switching (ZCS) and uses only one switching device. The computer simulation is given in order to conform the analytical work.

articleTitle: A Novel Robust Outlier Classification Founded On Localised Rank-Ordered Logarithmic Differences For Fix-Value Impulsive Noise
abstract: Outlier classification founded on Localised Rank Ordered Difference (LROD) technique, which is developed from Rank-Ordered Absolute Differences (ROAD), has been presented since 2015 therefore this LROD technique becomes one of the ultimate efficient outlier classification from its performance. This paper proposes the novel and robust outlier classification founded On LROLD (Localised Rank-Ordered Logarithmic Differences) technique, which is developed from LROD and Rank-Ordered Logarithmic Differences (ROLD), which is more efficient than LROD, for Fix-Value Impulsive Noise (FVIN). From the experimental simulation on three testing portraits: Girl, Pepper and Lena, the robust outlier classification founded on LROLD technique has the better efficiency than the previous techniques: LROD technique and ROAD technique at plentiful distribution of FVIN.

articleTitle: The Energy Meter Translation by Optical Character Recognition Technique
abstract: This paper presented an automatic energy meter reading system using the OCR process. Results showed that the system can recognize the energy meter reading digits in only three processes with an accuracy of 91 %. The work presented in this paper is a valuably consequential idea to design an algorithm of the energy meter translation using Optical Character Recognition (OCR).

articleTitle: Novel Innovation Design for Increasing Power Machine Using Mechanical Advantage Flywheel
abstract: This paper presents the design of novel innovation in electrical energy generation. It consists of permanent magnet synchronous generator, driven by motors through mechanical advantage flywheel. The mechanical advantage flywheel is designed to overcome the friction losses by momentum and mechanical advantage. It can increase the electrical energy from low power input to high power output. Therefore, it can increase low power from the distribution systems to the high power and supply to users. In addition, it can also increase the low power that is generated by renewable power plants to high power in order to distribute into the electrical distribution systems. The results indicated that the output power was up to 400.0% from the input power.

articleTitle: Development and Validation for Reentry Analysis Tool
abstract: In the last decades, the achievement in the research and developments of advanced space technology allows more satellites to be launched into the Earth orbits. It leads to an increasing number of space objects that can become threat to active satellites or humankind when they reentry the Earth. In 2018, Tiangong-1, for example, was discharged and planned to reentry the Earth. Thailand was one of many countries as the possible reentry area holding a high casualty risk. In this event, the Geo-Informatics and Space Technology Development Agency (GISTDA) was responsible for monitoring and analyzing the possible reentry areas and times using the flight dynamics analysis system known as "EMERALD". However, it requires an expert to perform more programming and analysis that is not convenient for the operators. This paper presents the reentry algorithm with an enhancement of the computational accuracy by applying special perturbations (the high-fidelity model of atmospheric drag and potential gravity). The enhanced algorithms were verified by comparing with the results from the Combined Space Operations Center (CSpOC) under the United States Strategic Command (USSTRATCOM). Then, the further development plan describes how to implement parallel computation technique to support the reentry analysis of over 21,000 space objects.

articleTitle: Frequency Estimation Based on Linear Predictor using Unbiased WLS Algorithm
abstract: An unbiased weighted least square (UWLS) adaptive algorithm is developed and proposed to cooperate with a second-order linear predictor to estimate the frequency of a single tone embed in noise. A new objective function and updating equations are introduced to improve the performance of previous WLS algorithm. Extensive simulations are drawn to verify the performance of the proposed estimator.

articleTitle: The Study of Bandwidth Expansion of Metamaterial Antenna Designed by Using Spiral Resonator
abstract: In the few years, the development of communication technology is rapidly. The metamaterial is interesting for radio frequency fielded researchers. Normally the metamaterial antenna behavior is narrowband. Therefore, the spiral resonator metamaterial antenna used for bandwidth expansion is presented in this work. The proposed antenna is designed by using a monopolar patch antenna with 2×4 different sizes of the spiral resonator (SR). Because the combination of four nearly interval resonant frequencies from 2×4 different sizes of SR make the resonant frequency around 1.7–2.63 GHz, the bandwidth is wider from 400 MHz to 930 MHz.

articleTitle: Recognition of Similar Gait Pattern Using Transfer Learning DarkNet
abstract: Nowadays, convolutional neural network as a recognition model has improved human identification by gait patterns. The model recognizes personal steps of walking and its performance is up to a training dataset. After a pre-processing for human segmentation, it shows that the gaits for each person are quite similar with no significant difference. This causes a low accuracy in the recognition. To solve this issue, this paper proposes DarkNet-19 model to improve human detection and is adapted to classify gait pattern by comparing in pixel levels. A new model is developed based on CASIA-B dataset. In the experimental results, a recognition rate and identification accuracy are increased. The proposed method enhances an ability to identify person, who is walking, carrying a backpack, and wearing a coat, of 99.83%, 98.10% and 99.85% respectively.

articleTitle: Unit Management of a BESS-Integrated Hydro Power Plant for Spinning Reserve Enhancement
abstract: Owing to its fast response, the hydro power plant is normally assigned to provide spinning reserve for the power system. Despite of its large capacity, minimum generation constraint and lack of management of multi-unit generations result in limited spinning reserve. This paper solves this problem by integrating a battery energy storage system with the hydro power plant and proposes a unit management algorithm to cooperatively manage the multi-unit generation. As a result, the hydro power plant can virtually provide any demanded generation, and its spinning reserve is increased significantly compared to the traditional operation. A case study on Rajjaprabha hydro power plant in Thailand is conducted to confirm feasibility of the proposed concept.

articleTitle: Feature Selection of 3D-Texture from MRI Data towards Localization of Prostate Tumor
abstract: Prostate cancer is the most common cancer in men in the EU. The TRUS-guided prostate biopsy e.g. is painful and lack accuracy. A noninvasive, reproducible and precise localization of prostate cancer without causing pain is still required. Multispectral MRI data of various modalities are currently promising technique for prostate cancer localization. However, it is obvious that these images are difficult to read. With the help of a computerized segmentation the time required to read the images could be reduced and the accuracy of eventual biopsies could be increased by focusing on a specific region. For this purpose, three major 3D textural features are exploited, i.e. GLCM, LBP, and three dimensional wavelet transform, together with T1-weighted, T2-weighted and contrast enhanced data will be used to generate a multispectral basis for the features. In this paper, all mentioned enhanced MRI features are investigated, at the end the best promising 3D features are presented.

articleTitle: Performance Characteristics of the Darrieus Wind Turbine with Battery Charging
abstract: Performance testing of the Darrieus wind turbine with battery charging was conducted in this paper. The turbine was investigated in terms of starting and power extraction performance. The investigation was made consequentially by considering the rotor performance, the generator performance, the power transmission between them through gear systems, and the effect of the battery load. It was found that the performance is strongly affected by the matching between the rotor, the generator, and the battery load through the gear systems. From all tests conducted, the turbine with a gear ratio of 1:3.61 which is connected to a 24V battery exhibits the maximum power output of 13.9 Watt.

articleTitle: Upper Sideband Improvement by Using Opened-end Stepped-impedance Resonator Filter Structure
abstract: A broad upper sideband improvement microstrip dual-mode resonator with stepped-impedance opened-end structure is represented to keep the dual-mode resonator's size compact size and lightweight. The stepped-impedance opened-end structure can change even mode resonant frequencies, whereas the odd mode frequency is fixed at the fundamental resonance. An improvement of the filter performance and wide suppress harmonics is achieved by locating transmission zero at the upper sideband. The simulated result of the dual-mode filter is designed at the resonant frequency of 2.14 GHz. The insertion loss is less than 1.1 dB, and the return loss better than 25 dB. It is exhibited that the upper sideband of dual-mode filter has a wide upper stopband, which improves from 15 dB to 25 dB over the frequency range of 2.1 GHz to 4.2 GHz compared to the conventional dual-mode structure.

articleTitle: The Development of a soil moisture measurement by using the high-frequency application
abstract: This paper presents the development of the soil moisture measurement using the high-frequency application. The simple technology with cheap equipment is implemented. We design and develop the software that can connect with the external equipment for sending and receiving the electromagnetic wave through the soil with different moisture. This application, therefore, can be applied in many applications such as agriculture and farming. The experiment of soil moisture measurement is conducted and the results are compared with the results obtained from the standard equipment with 3.4% of approximation error.

articleTitle: The Stability Analysis of the Aircraft Electric System with Regulated Buck-Boost Converter Unit
abstract: Generally, a regulated buck-boost converter unit behaves as a constant power loads. This load can corrupt the regarded system instability. Thus, stability analysis is very significant. In this paper, the eigenvalue theorem is suggested to diagnose the stability of the electric aircraft system with a regulated buck-boost converter unit. The results display that the offers model can affirm the unstable point predicted to the prepared model versus an eigenvalue theorem. Good acceptance between theory and simulation can be achieved.

articleTitle: Frequency Enhancement of Gigahertz Transverse Electromagnetic Cell for EMC Calibration in 300 kHz – 6 GHz
abstract: The objective of this research is to improve the 50-ohm load of Gigahertz Transverse Electromagnetic cell (GTEM cell) which is used for a specific broadband frequency of 300 kHz - 6 GHz using an impedance network matching technique known as resistive matching [9]. The improved GTEM cell is designed as a pyramid box that is composed of a parallel 50 Ohm impedance on a transmission line. The space inside the box is used to place a device under test (DUT). A thin conductor plate with in the box (Septum) is used to conduct electromagnetic wave. When a sinusoidal signal travels from a signal generator via the input port, the electric and magnetic signal are orthogonal in the transversal electro-magnetic mode (TEM mode). The magnitude of electromagnetic field under septum is stable without a disturbing electromagnetic signal from the outside box. The end of septum is connected to a 50ohm load to match with the impedance on the 50ohm input side. The results show that adjusting angle of the septum affects the reduction of the reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>). The RF absorbers are applied at the input port and the back of the GTEM cell to reduce the reflection of signal that has frequency over 1GHz. Finally, by these 50ohm impedance matching load improvement, the electric-field uniformity can be abtained within 300mm. x 300mm. x 200mm. test volume which complies to the IEC-61000-4 and IEEE139-2005 standards for electro-magnetic compatibility.

Author Keywords: Electromagnetic Wave Generator in Transversal Electro-Magnetic Mode

articleTitle: Design of EBG using Double Interdigital Coplanar Waveguide Structure for Reduced Size and High Gain Antenna
abstract: A new Mushroom-like Electromagnetic Band Gap (EBG) structure with double interdigital coplanar waveguide is proposed. The proposed structure has a fundamental frequency of 1.8 GHz and a size of λ/8. An array of 10×10 unit cells is designed to serve as a reflector to increase the gain of a dipole antenna. The antenna gain is increased to 7.98 dBi. The directivity of the antenna is increased to 7.82 dBi.
